The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 61, verse 1:

The whole universe is glorifying Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise. By placing this truth at the beginning of the surah, the believers are given the impression that your religion is the religion of this entire universe. And this religion is tawhid (the affirmation of Allah's oneness), and you are its trustees. The position of the disbelievers and polytheists is false, and they wish to extinguish the light of this religion. Allah is calling you to support this religion and this Messenger, and Allah has decreed the dominance of this religion. Although the disbelievers and polytheists wish to eliminate it, Allah has decided that He will make it prevail in spite of them. The meaning of this beginning is that this is the religion of the whole universe and the trust of the whole universe. The ideology for which you are to strive is the ideology of the whole universe, and the manifestation and dominance of this religion is in reality a natural matter, and the will and decree of Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.

After this, the believers are rebuked for displaying weakness on the part of some of them: whoever turns away from jihad in the cause of the religion, Allah greatly dislikes him and regards him as deserving of shame, especially from those who have believed, whereas Allah greatly loves those who strive in jihad in His way.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 61, verses 2-4:

"O you who believe! Why do you say what you do not do? It is most hateful in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do. Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks, as if they were a compact structure of lead." (61:2-4)

Ali ibn Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas that some of the Muslims, before the obligation of jihad, used to say: "Let Allah show us some deed that is most beloved to Him, so that we may act upon it." Allah informed the Prophet (ﷺ) that the most beloved deed to Allah is indeed faith, but after that, jihad against those who do not believe, disobey Allah and do not acknowledge faith is beloved to Allah. When the command of jihad was revealed, some Muslims disliked it and considered it a heavy command.

So Allah said: "O you who believe! Why do you say what you do not do?" (61:2-3)

Imam Ibn Jarir adopted this view in his tafsir.

However, Imam Ibn Kathir said: The majority of scholars have said that this verse was revealed when the Muslims wished that jihad be made obligatory, and when jihad became obligatory, some people disliked it. Something similar has also been mentioned elsewhere concerning this matter.

"Have you not seen those who were told, 'Restrain your hands, establish prayer and give zakah'? But when fighting was prescribed for them, a party of them feared men as they should fear Allah, or even more intensely. They said, 'Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You would delay us for a short term.' Say, 'The enjoyment of this world is brief, and the Hereafter is better for the one who fears Allah, and you will not be wronged even by the extent of a date-thread. Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers built up high.'" (4:77-78)

Qatadah and Dahhak said that this verse was revealed to rebuke those who said, "We killed, we shot, we struck," and similar things, when in fact they had not done so.

The context of the verse and the mention of fighting in it indicate that the view of the majority of the commentators is correct. This opinion was also adopted by Ibn Jarir. However, the meaning of Quranic verses is generally broader than the events of their revelation, indeed much broader. For this reason we take the general meaning and do not restrict it to the specific occasion of revelation. Yet it is necessary to keep in view the event in which the verse was revealed... The beginning takes the form that there is a rebuke upon an event or events.

"O you who believe! Why do you say what you do not do?" (61:2), and its conclusion is that with Allah this act is very hateful.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 61, verse 3:

"Kabura maqtan 'inda Allahi an taqooloo ma la taf'aloon" (16:2): "It is a most hateful thing in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do."

Al-Maqt (hatred, abhorrence): the disapproved matter that is extremely hateful in the sight of Allah. He regards it as very evil, and this is said by Allah, who is your Lord.

In the third verse, the matter that they had said they would do, but still fell short of in this regard, is clearly stated. It is jihad and qital (fighting). And it is declared that those who fight in ranks, arranged like a solid structure, are very beloved people.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 61, verse 4 (part 1 of 2):

Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks, as if they were a solid structure (bunyan marsus) of lead-fused wall. (61:4)

It is not merely fighting; rather the fighting must be in the cause of Allah, it must be organized, it must take place after order has been established within the ranks of society, and it must be carried out with the utmost steadfastness.

As we have stated in several surahs of this part, the Qur'an's aim was to build a community that would bear the trust of the Qur'an upon this earth. Its intention was to establish the Qur'anic way of life and to present the Qur'anic Shari'ah in the form of a complete system. For this purpose it was necessary to create a group and a society, and this very group had to be made into a practical group, and all of these tasks had to be undertaken together. It should be remembered that the nature of the Islamic system is that the worth of the individual lies in the group, not in isolation. Islam wishes to see its existence in the form of a closely interconnected and organized group, which has a system, which has a goal, and around which all its individuals revolve, such that this system is implemented in every person's conscience and in every person's action, and then on this earth in the practical form of a community, a society upon the surface of the earth in practical form, a community that is practically dynamic and carries out all its affairs within the limits and framework of this system.

Islam, although it places great emphasis on the reform of the individual, the reform of an individual's intention and the reform of conscience, and it is Islam that has given the principle of individual responsibility, yet Islam is not a religion of individuals, such that each one goes into his own place of worship and performs his own worship. In this way Islam cannot become a reality in the person of a single individual, nor can it become a reality in the person of a solitary individual. Islam has not come in the form of withdrawing into seclusion within one person's life; rather, the matter of Islam is that it should govern human life, exercise authority over life, control it, and dominate the individual and collective life and activities of people. This is because human beings do not live individually but live collectively, and since Islam has come to govern human beings, it is a collective system. That is why its etiquette, its rules, its intentions, and even its acts of worship are collective. If a command of Islam is for an individual, it is still for a person who is social and lives within a group, moves and sits within it, and within that group is a trustee of his religion, bearer of a system, and it is his duty to implement that system among people.

From the time the Prophet (ﷺ) began his call, the Islamic society began to be established, the formation of the Islamic group began, and Rasulullah (ﷺ) was declared the leader of this group. This group was one that had collective responsibilities and was completely distinct from its surroundings. It was taught such etiquette that if one end of it lay in the conscience of an individual, the other end was connected to the group, and this Islamic collective society existed even at the time when the Islamic government had not yet been established in Madinah; indeed, the Islamic government of Madinah was itself established through the Islamic group of Makkah.

When we reflect on these verses, the moral system built upon religious beliefs is both a collective necessity, and these morals can only manifest in the form of a collective system, and this system is such that to implement it there is a need for an administration.

In the first two verses, there is a rebuke that it does not befit a Muslim and a believer to say one thing and then not act upon it. This is a fundamental quality of the personality of a Muslim and a believer: truthfulness, steadfastness and uprightness. His inner and outer self should be one, his speech and action should be alike, and this matter is not restricted only to the issue of jihad; rather, a believer should be like this in every matter.

That a Muslim's outward and inward should be one, and that his speech and action should be alike, is a matter upon which the Qur'an has placed great emphasis, and it has stated this theme repeatedly. Concerning the Jews it was said:

"Do you enjoin righteousness upon the people while you forget yourselves, and you recite the Book? Do you not then use reason?" (2:44)

And while criticizing the hypocrites it has been said:

"And among the people is one whose speech about the worldly life pleases you, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the most hostile of enemies. When he gains authority, he strives throughout the earth to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals, and Allah does not like corruption." (2:204–205)

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted with something he betrays it." (Agreed upon)

There are many hadiths on this theme. The hadith that we mention next is among the most severe and stern guidance in this regard. Imam Ahmad narrated from Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Rabi'ah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to our house while I was a child. I set out to go outside to play. My mother said to me, "Abdullah, come here, I will give you something." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to my mother: "What did you intend to give him?" She said, "A date." He said: "If you had not done so, a lie would have been recorded against you." And this is why Imam Ahmad ibn Uqayl, travelling to a man to narrate a hadith (the journey being quite long), saw that man holding a bag and telling his mule that there was food in it, although it was empty; so Imam Ahmad deemed it unsuitable to narrate from that man, because he had lied to his mule.

This was the moral construction of Islam, this was the moral standard for a Muslim, and these were the people who were made the trustees of the Islamic way of life. This standard is the purpose and axis of this surah, and it is an important point in the training of the Islamic group, which Allah takes up to rectify the Islamic way.

When we come to the principal subject, which is the axis and theme of this surah, namely jihad fi sabilillah, we find before us several topics so that we may reflect upon them and take a lesson from them.

First of all, before us stands the self of the human being, and this self experiences moments of weakness. Only Allah can protect it from this weakness, and constant reminder and constant training are needed. In the narrations it is recorded that these were some of the very earliest emigrants, who wished that permission be given to them to fight. These people were in Makkah, and their zeal was such that they wished to fight right there in Makkah; but at that time they were commanded to restrain their hands, to establish prayer and to give zakat. However, when jihad was made obligatory upon them, and that too in Madinah and at the appropriate time, some of them began to fear people as one ought to fear Allah, and even more so. And they began to say:

"Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You would delay us for a short term." (4:77)

Or it was a group of Madinah itself, which asked about the most beloved deeds, and when it was told that the most beloved deed is jihad fi sabilillah, they disliked it.

This single incident is sufficient to open our eyes: that the human self is very weak and needs continuous training, reminder and admonition day and night, especially when it is being given the most difficult target. This training is necessary so that it keeps walking correctly on its path, overcomes its weaknesses, and keeps its gaze fixed on the distant high horizon. Furthermore, from this we also learn that a Muslim should never be impatient to take on a difficult target; and when the desire is for the religion, one should thank Allah. If we present proposals before Allah and Allah were to present us with those circumstances, perhaps we would not remain steadfast. Look: this is the first community of Muslims, and even among them there were people upon whom a rebuke was directed: why do you say things that you do not act upon? This is a severe reproach and a frightening censure.

The second matter that comes to the fore is that Allah loves those who fight in His way, as if they were a solid structure. How forcefully Allah urges the Muslims to fight in His path, yet the record shows that this emphasis was made to remove the psychological state of some people who disliked war and wished to postpone it and were withdrawing from battle. Therefore they were firmly urged here. But the specific occasion of revelation does not mean that this verse is only for particular circumstances; rather, it is the general policy of Islam that people should be kept ready for war circumstances at all times.

An important point is that Islam does not want to create a war-frenzy needlessly, nor does it regard war as a beloved thing. Islam makes war obligatory because circumstances compel it. Then the purposes for which Islam wages war are lofty purposes. Islamic war is fought so that Allah's final way of life may be implemented and established in Islamic lands. Although this Islamic way of life is a natural way of life, Islam also imposes responsibilities upon human souls to raise themselves to the standard of this way, so that this system may remain established at that high standard. Yet it is also a practical reality that on this earth there have always been forces whose aim is that the Islamic way of life should not take root in this world, because the non-Islamic systems of the world have certain interests and privileges; these systems are founded upon some false and hollow values. Whenever an Islamic system has been established in the world, the interests of such forces have come to an end. These false ways of life exploit the weaknesses of human souls, and by dragging people down from the human level, creating moral corruption within them, and keeping them ignorant of the truth, they set them up in opposition to the Islamic system. Thus the common people, out of their ignorance, begin to block the path of Islam. Polytheism is dominant and falsehood appears swollen, and the schemes of Satan are very deep. This is why the Qur'an prescribes a high moral standard for the bearers of faith and the guardians and custodians of the Islamic way of life, so that they may confront the agents of evil and Satan well. Their moral condition should be strong, so that they can fight against the enemies, and they should always be ready for such a war as the enemies of Islam may impose upon them. This alone is the guarantee by which the path of the Islamic call is not blocked, through which the Islamic system is maintained, and people receive freedom of expression, and are able to establish the system of their own choice.

Then these people do jihad and qital in the way of Allah; they do not fight for their own selves, nor do they fight for any kind of partisanship: neither for racial, nor linguistic, nor regional, nor tribal partisanship. They fight only in the way of Allah, so that the Word of Allah may be exalted. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "One who fights only so that the Word of Allah is exalted, he is fighting in the way of Allah."

The meaning of "Kalimat Allah" is that Allah's commands and purposes be served; and it is also Allah's will that just as this entire universe glorifies Allah and moves according to Allah's law of nature, so too humanity should move according to the final and complete system of life and divine Shari'ah sent by Allah. Thus this whole universe and all the human beings within it should move according to Allah's law, and the law and Shari'ah of no one other than Allah should prevail.

It was necessary that certain individuals obstruct the system of Shari'ah, that certain classes not allow the Islamic system to be established, and that certain governments regard it as a threat to themselves; and there was no alternative except that Islam should overcome these obstacles and confront them. This is why jihad and qital were made obligatory upon the Muslims, so that the Islamic system could be established and preserved, and so that the Word of Allah might be exalted upon the earth. This is why Allah loves those who array themselves in ranks in His way, as if they were a solid structure.

This is the condition upon which we should reflect deeply.

Those who fight in His cause in ranks, as if they were a solid structure cemented with lead (61:4). If the mujahideen are not in this state, they may not be beloved. This is a command both for each individual and for the collective. That is, they should be such that they form a community with a firmly organised system. This is because the forces that obstruct the path of Islam take the form of organised and collective strength, and they gather their full strength against it. Therefore it is also an obligation on the forces of Islam to come out gathered against their enemies, and to emerge as a single nation. They should come out like a solid wall and in a highly organised form, coming out in harmony. Hence the notion that a single person alone worships Allah, alone fights jihad, and alone conducts his life is a state that goes against the very temperament of this religion, goes against the demands of the state of jihad, and goes against the form that governs the whole of life thereafter.

This picture which Allah, the Exalted, presents here for the Muslims is in reality a picture of the religion of the Muslims. This picture shows what the signposts of the path of the Muslims are, and how the Qur'an prescribes for them a collective system of support and protection.

"In a rank, as if they were a solid structure cemented with lead" (61:4). A wall whose bricks are joined together, bonded to one another, with every brick performing its duty and every brick standing in its place performing its duty. If even one brick is removed, the entire building may collapse. Likewise, if a brick moves forward, moves back, or the upper brick separates from the lower brick, a breach may appear in the wall. All these matters define the mutual bond of the members of the community, who advance in one direction. That is, they should be in harmony with one another consciously, march together in thought and outlook, be organised in their system, just as the beads of a rosary are, and their target should also be one.

Following this, the story of Musa (peace be upon him) is narrated, showing that the method of the Islamic revolution has been one and the same in all the callings, from Adam (peace be upon him) onward.

The Children of Israel harming Musa, even though he was the one who was to deliver them and this nation from the oppression of Pharaoh, and he was their messenger, leader and teacher, points to a story consisting of continuous harm inflicted upon him. The hardships and difficult stages that he passed through in order to set this people right constitute tireless struggle. The Qur'an has given its details in abundance, and on reading them a person accepts that this was tireless struggle and that he was among the Messengers of firm resolve (Ulu al-Azm).

Their condition was this: Musa (peace be upon him) was striving to free them from humiliation and confronting the grip and tyranny of Pharaoh, yet these people did not like to live in peace and tranquillity even in that state; in that condition they used to criticise Musa (peace be upon him). They would pass comment on this tireless struggle.

They said: ﴿You harmed us before you came to us, and after you have come﴾ (7:129). That is, they were not seeing any good for themselves in his mission; rather, they regarded that mission as the cause of their harm.

But as soon as Allah drowned Pharaoh and saved the Children of Israel, and they witnessed this entire scene with their own eyes, upon being saved they resolved to abandon the monotheistic call of Musa (peace be upon him), and, like the people of Pharaoh, resolved to commit shirk.

﴿So they passed on, and came upon a people who were devoted to some idols of theirs. They said: "O Musa, make for us a god just as they have gods"﴾ (7:138). That is, they came upon a people devoted to a few of their idols, and said: "O Musa, make for us also a god like the gods they have."

Musa (peace be upon him) went up the mountain for his Lord's meeting, from where he was given the tablets of the Torah. As soon as he left, the Samiri led them astray.

﴿And the Samiri brought forth for them a calf, a body that lowed. They said: "This is your god and the god of Musa, but he [Musa] forgot"﴾ (20:88). That is, the Samiri fashioned for them a calf of an image from which came the sound of a cow's lowing. The people cried out: "This is your god and the god of Musa. Musa has forgotten him."

Then they began raising objections to the food that they received in the wilderness in the form of manna and quails, and said:

﴿O Musa, we will not endure one kind of food; so call upon your Lord to bring forth for us of what the earth grows—its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils and its onions﴾ (2:61).

After this, when they were commanded to slaughter a cow, they resorted to pretexts and impertinence. This impertinence was against the Prophet and also against the Lord, the Exalted. They said: call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what she is like, what her colour is.

﴿So they slaughtered her, though they had nearly not done it﴾ (2:71). That is, they slaughtered her, though they did not appear to be doing it.

After this they themselves demanded the Sabbath as a day of rest, and then violated it. Then they were commanded to enter the holy land which Allah had prescribed for them, but they refused to enter the sacred land, humiliated and abased.

﴿They said: "O Musa, indeed in it are a mighty people, and we will never enter it until they leave it. But if they leave, then we will enter"... they said: "O Musa, we will never enter it as long as they are within it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are sitting right here"﴾ (5:22–24). They said: "O Musa, there are very powerful people there, and we will never go there until they leave it; if they leave, then we are ready to enter." And when Musa (peace be upon him) insisted, their answer was: "O Musa, we will never go there as long as they are there. So you and your Lord go and fight; we are sitting right here."

Apart from this, through repeated disobedience, questions, rebellion and personal accusations, these people repeatedly harmed Musa (peace be upon him). The details of which come in the hadith.

Here Allah relates the saying of Musa (peace be upon him), which in a tone of affection is a complaint against them:

﴿O my people, why do you harm me, when you certainly know that I am the Messenger of Allah to you?﴾ (61:5). And they had no doubt that Musa (peace be upon him) was the Messenger of Allah. Yet their saying is a complaint that contains both reproach and advice.

But when they disregarded all the efforts of reform and steadfastness, Allah further turned their hearts crooked, and these hearts became no longer fit for guidance. They went astray, and Allah also decreed misguidance for them.

﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ (61:5). Thus their steadfastness in the religion ended, the office of the guardians of the religion was taken from them, and they remained upon that crooked path and misguidance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 61, verses 6–7:

Then Jesus, son of Mary, came and said to the Children of Israel: "O Children of Israel, I am the Messenger of Allah sent to you" (61:6). He did not say that he was God, nor that he was the son of God, nor that he was one hypostasis (aqnum) among the hypostases of Allah.

"Confirming the Torah that came before me, and giving good news of a Messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad" (61:6). In such clear words the picture of prophethood is presented: the chain of prophethood is one, and every Messenger who comes after another Messenger confirms the prophethood of the one before him. Thus the circles of one prophethood extend between heaven and earth and over the long history of the earth, and they are joined to one another, and this is the picture worthy of Allah's method of truth. It is one religion and one method. This form has differed for different peoples, because humanity differed across different ages in knowledge, experience and capacity, so the form of the Shariah also differed. But to the final Prophet, ﷺ, was given a mature intellect, so he was given a final and complete Shariah. A mature nation with a firm intellect was given a complete Shariah. This religion appealed to human reason and left a wide field of action for reason to work within, yet a boundary of action was definitively fixed for all humanity so that it might work within it, and the determination of that boundary was made by the Creator of the universe Himself, looking at human strength and capacity.

From this verse it is apparent that the prophecy of Ahmad was present in the Gospel, whether or not it is present in the Gospels in circulation today, because it has been established that the present Gospels were written in later periods, and the circumstances in which they were written are also known.

When the Qur'an was revealed in the Arabian Peninsula, the Jews and Christians also read it, in which was: "the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel" (7:157). Some sincere scholars among them acknowledged this, as did Abdullah ibn Salam, because these people were keen to conceal this verse.

Furthermore, historical reports are consistent that the Jews awaited this final Prophet, ﷺ, and they also believed that his time had come near. Likewise, some of the Christians who were monotheists and scattered here and there in the Arabian Peninsula also confirmed it. But the Jews, who had hoped that this final Prophet would be from among them, when Allah sent him from the second branch of the descendants of Ibrahim, Bani Isma'il, disliked it greatly and began war against him.

In any case, the Qur'anic text itself is definitive on this matter, and the Qur'an alone is a trustworthy source, in which no alteration occurs, whereas the state of the Torah and the Gospel is known to all.

Accordingly, according to most exegetical opinions, the following verses concern how the Jews and Christians received the Prophet whose good news was given in their own books. In these verses their conduct is severely condemned: instead of welcoming this religion, they began conspiring against it, although Allah's decision is that this religion will prevail over all religions and that it is the final religion.

"But when he came to them with clear signs, they said, 'This is clear magic'" (61:6). "Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah while he is being invited to Islam (submission to Allah)? Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it. It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it" (61:6–9).

The Children of Israel stood in opposition to this new religion. They began enmity, conspiracies and misleading propaganda, and brought every kind of base weapon against it, and the war they began against this religion has not ended to this day. First of all they leveled this accusation against it:

"When he came to them with clear signs, they said, 'This is manifest sorcery'" (61:6). Just as those who did not know the scriptures or the good news said the same. The conduct of the People of the Book and of non-People of the Book remained one and the same. Indeed, the People of the Book even began conspiracies within the Islamic front: they tried to set the Muhajirun and the Ansar against each other, and tried to set the two Ansari tribes, Aws and Khazraj, against each other. At times they united with the Meccan polytheists to wage war against this new religion, and at other times they sought to fight against it in alliance with the hypocrites of Medina. They supported every aggressor against Medina and the Muslim world. For example, in the Battle of the Confederates (Ghazwa al-Ahzab) they took an active part, and they participated by raising false accusations. In the incident of the slander (ifk) they amplified it through Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and in the Fitna of Uthman they worked through Abdullah ibn Saba. Then, through an organized conspiracy, they introduced Israelite narratives (Isra'iliyyat) into the books of Sira. When they became unable to insert fabricated verses into the Qur'an, they sought to insert fabricated hadiths into tafsir, sira and hadith literature.

This war against Islam has not ended to this day. Even today, global Judaism, global Christianity and Zionism are busy day and night with conspiracies against Islam. They attack Islam from every side and incite people to wage war against Islam. In this war there has been neither ceasefire nor peace for fourteen hundred years, in no era whatsoever. In the East they fought the Crusades. In the West, in Andalusia, they erased the name and trace of the Muslims. In the Middle East they always waged war against the Islamic caliphate. Until they destroyed the Turkish caliphate and reduced it to pieces. Even after this their war did not end, and they produced false "heroes" for the Islamic world and the Muslim world, and through them quenched their thirst for vengeance against Islam. When they wished to shatter the last sign of Islam, the Islamic caliphate of Turkey, they raised up a great hero in Turkey and inflated him with such air that he became a very great leader. Afterwards the armies of the Allies, who had conquered Istanbul (Astana), retreated before him, so that this man could be presented as a great conqueror, a conqueror who could shatter the Islamic caliphate into pieces. He separated Turkey from the Islamic world. He declared that Turkey was a secular state and had no connection with religion. Whenever the Jews wish to strike at Islam, they produce leaders of this kind for the Islamic world; whenever they strike at true Islamic movements, they produce leaders of this kind in Muslim countries, and through them they raise in those countries every kind of partisanship other than Islamic zeal and Islamic solidarity, and they raise every banner other than the Islamic banner.

In any case, the Qur'anic text itself is definitive on this matter, and the Qur'an alone is a trustworthy source, in which no alteration occurs, whereas the state of the Torah and the Gospel is known to all.

Accordingly, according to most exegetical opinions, the following verses concern how the Jews and Christians received the Prophet whose good news was given in their own books. In these verses their conduct is severely condemned: instead of welcoming this religion, they began conspiring against it, although Allah's decision is that this religion will prevail over all religions and that it is the final religion.

"But when he came to them with clear signs, they said, 'This is clear magic'" (61:6). "Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah while he is being invited to Islam (submission to Allah)? Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it. It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it" (61:6–9).

The Children of Israel stood in opposition to this new religion. They began enmity, conspiracies and misleading propaganda, and brought every kind of base weapon against it, and the war they began against this religion has not ended to this day. First of all they leveled this accusation against it:

"When he came to them with clear signs, they said, 'This is manifest sorcery'" (61:6). Just as those who did not know the scriptures or the good news said the same. The conduct of the People of the Book and of non-People of the Book remained one and the same. Indeed, the People of the Book even began conspiracies within the Islamic front: they tried to set the Muhajirun and the Ansar against each other, and tried to set the two Ansari tribes, Aws and Khazraj, against each other. At times they united with the Meccan polytheists to wage war against this new religion, and at other times they sought to fight against it in alliance with the hypocrites of Medina. They supported every aggressor against Medina and the Muslim world. For example, in the Battle of the Confederates (Ghazwa al-Ahzab) they took an active part, and they participated by raising false accusations. In the incident of the slander (ifk) they amplified it through Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and in the Fitna of Uthman they worked through Abdullah ibn Saba. Then, through an organized conspiracy, they introduced Israelite narratives (Isra'iliyyat) into the books of Sira. When they became unable to insert fabricated verses into the Qur'an, they sought to insert fabricated hadiths into tafsir, sira and hadith literature.

This war against Islam has not ended to this day. Even today, global Judaism, global Christianity and Zionism are busy day and night with conspiracies against Islam. They attack Islam from every side and incite people to wage war against Islam. In this war there has been neither ceasefire nor peace for fourteen hundred years, in no era whatsoever. In the East they fought the Crusades. In the West, in Andalusia, they erased the name and trace of the Muslims. In the Middle East they always waged war against the Islamic caliphate. Until they destroyed the Turkish caliphate and reduced it to pieces. Even after this their war did not end, and they produced false "heroes" for the Islamic world and the Muslim world, and through them quenched their thirst for vengeance against Islam. When they wished to shatter the last sign of Islam, the Islamic caliphate of Turkey, they raised up a great hero in Turkey and inflated him with such air that he became a very great leader. Afterwards the armies of the Allies, who had conquered Istanbul (Astana), retreated before him, so that this man could be presented as a great conqueror, a conqueror who could shatter the Islamic caliphate into pieces. He separated Turkey from the Islamic world. He declared that Turkey was a secular state and had no connection with religion. Whenever the Jews wish to strike at Islam, they produce leaders of this kind for the Islamic world; whenever they strike at true Islamic movements, they produce leaders of this kind in Muslim countries, and through them they raise in those countries every kind of partisanship other than Islamic zeal and Islamic solidarity, and they raise every banner other than the Islamic banner.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 61, verse 8:

﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will not allow His light to be extinguished, though the disbelievers may dislike it.﴾ (61:8) This verse expresses this great truth. And this truth is presented in the form of an image that naturally moves a person to laugh at the condition of these people. They used to level the accusation with their mouths that this is clear magic, they used to plot against it, and they wanted to end it through secret schemes and to finish off this new religion. Therefore, against their plots, Allah drew this disappointing picture of them: that they wish to extinguish the light of Allah with the puffs of their mouths. The light of Allah, and these weak and contemptible ones!

﴿And Allah will complete His light, though the disbelievers may dislike it.﴾ (61:8) Allah will fully spread His light, even if it is disliked by the disbelievers. The promise of Allah proved true. Allah spread His light completely during the lifetime of the Prophet (ﷺ). He established an Islamic community, a very vibrant and radiant Islamic community, and gave it the Islamic system of life with very clear signs, and determined its limits and bounds. For generations this ideology remained alive and active in the practical lives of people, not merely in books; Allah made it dominant in the realm of reality. Allah the Most Holy completed that light, the religion of the Muslims was perfected, and He completed His favours upon the Muslims and chose Islam as their religion. He made this religion beloved to them, and they fought for it, to the extent that if a Muslim were thrown into fire, he would prefer it over returning to disbelief. Thus the form of the religion was completed in the hearts of people. And after you too, this situation has arisen from time to time and has endured, even though from every side there have been plots, attacks and persecutions against the Muslims. Despite attacks from every direction, Islam comes to life after every Karbala, because Islam is the light of Allah, and human efforts cannot extinguish the light of Allah. Neither fire nor iron can destroy it. However, the artificial leaders of the Islamic world, who are the self-appointed leaders of the Jews and Christians, sometimes think that they have ended Islam and extinguished its light. As stated above, Allah's decree was that the light of God would spread and the religion would prevail.

Qur'an 61:9 (Urdu): ﴿It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it.﴾ (16 : 9)

This is testimony that the Islamic way of life is guidance and the religion of truth. It is a decisive matter, and nothing can be added to it. The will of Allah has been fulfilled, and this religion has prevailed over all other religions. In its essence and its make-up, this religion is unique; there is no religion comparable to it. For example, among the idolatrous religions of the world, there is no question of competition at all. As for the religions of the Book, this is the final and complete religion in the same line, and it is the last edition of Allah's system. It exists in its complete and sublime form.

The earlier divine scriptures have been subjected to countless distortions (tahrif, alteration). Their form has been changed, they have been broken into pieces, and additions have been made to them that were not there originally. They have been edited and cut. They have reached a state in which they can no longer provide guidance for the life of the modern age. Even if it is accepted that no distortion occurred in them, they are still earlier editions, whereas the religion of Islam is the final and most recent copy of Allah's system, in which all the problems of advanced modern life have been resolved. The earlier religions came for a limited period according to Allah's plan.

Allah's promise has been fulfilled in respect of the religion itself, its nature, and its laws and content, in that there is no religion equal to Islam. Yet this system has also remained a dominant system in practical life. This religion has indeed prevailed once. It spread so widely over this earth that all religions and all nations remained under its sway for approximately one hundred years. After that too, this religion spread like a flood through Central Asia and Central Africa. Moreover, through the early jihadi struggle, a number of people entered it, and after that, through tabligh (propagation) alone, this religion spread by its own inner strength to five times the area and population. Even today, this religion is spreading without the support of state power. Yet, through the conspiracy of the Jews and Zionists, the political system of the people of religion, the caliphate system, has been abolished. This system was ended in Turkey by the hands of a "hero" whom they had themselves fabricated for this purpose. And despite the fact that conspiracies against this religion are taking place day and night throughout the Muslim world, and the "heroes" installed by the Jews throughout the Muslim world are crushing the Islamic movements arising in the Muslim world, this is Allah's lamp, and it cannot be extinguished by blowing on it.

In short, despite the conspiracies of both its own people and outsiders, this religion still plays an important role in human history, and it has played such a role before as well. Human conspiracies cannot block its path, because the power of man is no power in the face of Allah. Even if they devise very deep schemes, Allah also devises deep plans.

These verses were encouraging the believers at a time when the early audience of the Qur'an was striving for the victory of the religion in spite of the efforts and conspiracies of the Jews and Christians. Even then, Allah was making the religion prevail; the Muslims were merely a veil and a pretext for the hand of divine power. Today too, these verses are creating courage for those who are working for the supremacy of the religion, and in the future they will serve as a guiding light for movements that arise to establish the religion's supremacy. The day is not far when this religion will once again prevail.

After the description of the Islamic worldview and its continuity, and after the promise that this religion must prevail, even if the disbelievers plot against it, the address now turns to the Muslims. It is addressed to the Muslims of that time, and also to the Muslims who will come until the Day of Resurrection: O Muslims, according to this religion, an excellent trade is being pointed out to you, and that trade is jihad in the way of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 61, verse 10:

"O you who believe! Shall I direct you to a commerce that will save you from a painful punishment? Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you only knew. He will forgive you your sins and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, and into pleasant dwellings in the gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great success. And there is another thing you desire: help from Allah and a near victory. So give good tidings to the believers." (61:10-13)

Notice the manner of expression here. Some elements are joined together, while others are kept apart from their place. There is a gap between the question and the answer to the question. Some things are placed first and others are delayed. The purpose of all these features is only that this call and this voice sink deeply into people's hearts, and that by employing every means of expressive style, the matter is conveyed to the hearts, indeed to the very depths of the hearts.

Look at the beginning of the call.

"Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū" (61:10), "O you who believe!" Then Allah asks them: "Shall I direct you to a commerce?" This creates a powerful eagerness in the hearts of the listeners.

"Hal adullukum ... 'adhābin alīm" (61:10), "Shall I direct you to a commerce that will save you from a painful punishment?"

Now, who would not be eager to learn about such a commerce? But here the verse ends and a pause occurs in the middle. Between the question and the answer to the question, the verse concludes and a pause comes, and eagerness to hear the next verse arises in the listener's heart. Then the answer comes, when the listeners were already eager.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 61, verse 11:

"Believe in Allah and His Messenger" (61:11). They had already believed in Allah and His Messenger. When they hear this answer, their hearts are illuminated, because the condition of this answer already exists within them.

"And strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives" (61:11). This is the theme and the central axis of this surah. It recurs in this manner, again and again, and is repeated within the subject matter in this way. This is because Allah knew that to train a human being, repeated reminders are needed, with various kinds of proofs and various forms of reinforcement and emphasis, so that the human soul becomes prepared to perform such burdensome duties. For without the performance of these kinds of burdensome duties, the Islamic methodology can neither survive here nor be preserved. After this, further comment is made on this trade, and this trade is praised and commended.

"That is better for you, if you only knew" (61:11). This is because a person moves towards any good only when he knows that this is the good. After this, in the following verses, further details of this good and this trade are given, because after a general statement, the effect of details is very great. In this way the matter settles firmly in the feelings.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 61, verse 12:

﴿يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ﴾ (16:21) "Allah will forgive you your sins." This one matter alone is sufficient for this trade and goodness. If after this anyone should still want his sins forgiven, or what else would he store up for himself? But the bounties and mercy of Allah have no limits, therefore:

﴿وَيُدْخِلْكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ﴾ "And He will admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and will grant you excellent dwellings in gardens of everlasting residence." What greater trade is there than that a mujahid, in this brief life of his, strives in jihad, gives up his life, and in return receives these gardens and eternal life, and dwells in excellent homes and everlasting bliss? And this is a great reality: this is indeed the great success.

﴿ذَٰلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾ (16:21) "That is the great triumph." Here this most profitable trade comes to its conclusion. Indeed, this is a very great gain: that a believer gives a limited world and takes an eternal Hereafter. If someone trades one rupee and earns ten, his fame spreads in the marketplace; but what then will be the state of the one who strives in this limited worldly life, gives up its limited goods, and enjoys the unlimited span of the Hereafter, obtaining the provision and pleasure of the Hereafter, which is unbounded and unending?

This transaction took place between the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and Abdullah ibn Rawahah ؓ. It took place on the night of ʿAqabah. They said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he should set whatever conditions he wished for himself. Then the Noble Messenger ﷺ said: "For the Lord, I impose this condition: that you worship Him and associate no one with Him. And for myself, I impose this condition: that you will defend me in the same way that you defend your own property and lives." They said: "If we do this, what will we get?" He ﷺ said: (Paradise). They said: "In this transaction a great benefit has come to us; we neither cancel this transaction nor accept the request of the other party in this regard."

But the grace of Allah is very great. Allah knows that human souls desire something in this world as well. The limited constitution of man wishes to find some delight in this world too, so Allah Ta'ala gives them the glad tidings that in this world too you will attain a manifest victory and the dominance of the religion, and the Islamic system of life will be established, and it will be established among your progeny.

"And another [favour] that you love: help from Allah and a near victory. So give good news to the believers." ﴿وَأُخْرَىٰ تُحِبُّونَهَا ۖ نَصْرٌ مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَفَتْحٌ قَرِيبٌ ۗ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (16:31)

This commerce reaches the limits of the rate of profit, and this profit can only be given by Allah. He is Allah, whose treasures have no shortage, and He is Allah, whose mercy no one can withhold. What are these mercies? Forgiveness of sins, gardens, and excellent dwellings in which there will be everlasting blessings. And the profit of this bargain is not only in the Hereafter; a portion of it is also given here in this world: Allah's help, dominance of the religion, and a manifest victory. Who would not engage in such a trade, or hesitate over it, or turn away from it?

After this encouragement and exhortation comes a picture of the concept of the human self. This concept is very important for a human being. A person who holds the faith-based concept of this universe and of this life within it, and who lives his life while holding this concept in his heart, and who also has the broad horizons and limits of this concept, if he then thinks about a life that is empty of faith, a life that is extremely limited, narrow and small, whose level is very low, and whose most important matters are extremely worthless, then a heart which has seen these vast expanses of faith cannot remain alive even for a minute in such a limited and worthless life. It will not delay even a single minute in joining that struggle and striving whose aim is to establish on this earth such an expansive life, so that he may live in it, and so that people may also live in it. Moreover, the situation is such that he does not seek any reward for this struggle and striving, because this life and this system are themselves an aim and a reward. Who can abandon this struggle, which fills the heart with joy and delight, and who can live without it? Such a person rushes and plunges into this struggle. Even if it is the fire of Nimrod, he plunges in; whatever the outcome, he plunges in.

But observe: Allah knows that the human self is very weak, and at any time its fervour and enthusiasm may decline, and that the sharpness of the struggle may dull at any moment, and that the love of ease and preference for comfort may at some time incline a person to live a lowly life. Therefore the Noble Qur'an does not finish by speaking in only one style. It strives from every aspect to prepare the human self. It gives every kind of influence, argument, evidence and example. It calls repeatedly, and it does not leave a person merely to faith and individual [efforts], nor does it give a single command and be done with it, the way a government official issues a circular.

Thus the surah concludes with a new call. This call has a fresh tone: a modern argument, an effective example, and an exhortation and incitement from a new angle.

"O you who believe, be helpers of Allah, as Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples: 'Who will be my helpers for Allah?' The disciples replied: 'We are Allah's helpers.' Then a group of the Children of Israel believed, and another group disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemies, and they became the dominant ones." (61:14)

Who were the disciples (hawariyyun)? They were the students of Jesus (peace be upon him). They numbered 21. They were always with him and took teachings from him. It was these very people who, after he was raised, spread his counsels and his teachings.

The purpose of the verse is not to narrate their life circumstances, but to present the stance they took regarding the call (da'wah). Therefore we too content ourselves here with that.

"O you who believe, be helpers of Allah" (61:14). See to what lofty station Allah raises His striving servants. What greater station can a human being have than to become a helper of Allah? In this quality there is an honour so great that it surpasses even Paradise and its bounties. Become the helpers of Allah!

As He said: "As Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples: 'Who will be my helpers for Allah?' And the disciples replied: 'We are Allah's helpers.'" They dedicated themselves to this task and attained this station of honour. And among the duties of Jesus (peace be upon him) was to give glad tidings of the final Prophet, Muhammad (ﷺ), and to announce the good news of the final religion. Therefore the followers of Muhammad (ﷺ) are more deserving that they advance for this task, just as the disciples offered themselves. This is the element of encouragement and incitement in this matter. And then, what was the outcome?

"Then a group of the Children of Israel believed, and another group disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemies, and they became the dominant ones" (61:14). This verse can have two meanings. One is that those who believed in the prophethood of Jesus, that is, the Christians, whether their beliefs were correct or whether they later became polytheists and their beliefs suffered severe deviations, were made dominant by Allah over those who did not accept the prophethood of Jesus (peace be upon him), namely the Jews, as history bears witness. The second meaning can be that those who believed in his prophethood and remained steadfast on the belief in Tawhid and the humanity of the Messenger, Allah supported these people of Tawhid by the power of their proof and argument, in contrast to those who became polytheists and who regarded Jesus as God, or regarded his mother as divine, or regarded the Holy Spirit as God. Then these people of Tawhid were also supported through the Islamic doctrine of Tawhid, and the religion of Jesus became dominant in the form of the religion of Islam. This second interpretation is the more appropriate.

The lesson intended by this allusion and this event is the one we stated above: preparing the believers for jihad in the way of Allah, which is the axis of this surah. For the believers are responsible for establishing the religion of Allah. They are the heirs of the final message. They are the people who have been brought forth for this great purpose. They should fulfil this and their life's duty.

"As Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples: Who will be my helpers in calling to Allah? And the disciples replied: We are Allah's helpers." And victory and triumph in the Hereafter belong to those who are Allah's helpers and servants of His religion.

This is the final call of this surah. It is the final pinch and the final incitement. It has its own colour and distinct flavour, and this example is most suitable to the theme of this surah: a historical example and a historical hue.
